lessons.title: Say hello
lessons.canDo: Start and end a friendly conversation.
lessons.scenario: You and Smarty meet Mia and Sam at the classroom door. Practise starting and ending a conversation; no personal details are needed.

items.note: Hello and Hi start a conversation. Goodbye ends it. Hi is more informal.

practice.prompt: Start the conversation with a greeting, rather than ending it.
practice.explanation: Hello is a complete greeting. Use it when you meet someone.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Hi is a short, friendly way to say hello.

practice.prompt: Build the taught phrase in its natural word order.
practice.explanation: Goodbye ends the conversation.

practice.prompt: Say a short goodbye to Smarty. Complete the phrase.
practice.explanation: Bye and Goodbye both end a conversation. Bye is the shorter form.

practice.prompt: You are speaking to Smarty for the first time. Choose the greeting addressed to Smarty.
practice.explanation: Address Smarty by name. Hi, Mia addresses a different person; Goodbye ends the conversation.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: You have greeted someone in English. You can also say Hi, Smarty!

practice.prompt: Mia greets you with Hi. Choose a greeting back, not a goodbye.
practice.explanation: You can reply to a greeting with another greeting.

practice.prompt: Build the longer goodbye to Sam.
practice.explanation: Goodbye ends the conversation.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Bye is a short goodbye. Listen to the first word.

story.hook: Who gives Smarty a short goodbye?

questions.explanation: Find the line with the name or phrase in the question.
Use the speaker labels and the actual words in the dialogue.
Find the matching line in the dialogue; use what the story actually says.

image.describe: A bright classroom door where Smarty the black cat waves hello while Mia and Sam stand smiling beside him.

mission.setup: You and Smarty meet Mia and Sam at the classroom door. Practise starting and ending a conversation; no personal details are needed.

turns.hint: Greet Smarty. Hello and Hi both work.
End with Goodbye or Bye.

lessons.title: Tell me your name
lessons.canDo: Introduce yourself and recognise a name question.
lessons.scenario: A new classmate asks what to call you. Choose an imaginary name or nickname, then ask their name back.

items.note: My name is… and I’m… both introduce you. I’m is the short form of I am. Use a nickname or an imaginary name if you prefer. My name is Mia means the speaker is called Mia.

grammar.title: Two ways to introduce yourself
grammar.explanation: My name is… and I’m… both introduce you. I’m is the short form of I am. Use a nickname or an imaginary name if you prefer.

practice.prompt: Introduce yourself as Mia using My name is.
practice.explanation: My name is + a name. My tells us the name belongs to the speaker.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: I am Sam and I’m Sam both introduce the speaker as Sam. Listen for the name after am.

practice.prompt: Build the taught phrase in its natural word order.
practice.explanation: What’s your name? asks what to call you.

practice.prompt: Introduce yourself as Mia. Complete the introduction.
practice.explanation: My name is + a name. My tells us the name belongs to the speaker.

practice.prompt: Match each full form to its short form. They have the same meaning.
practice.explanation: The short forms express the same meaning as their full forms. The apostrophe marks missing letters.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: Say the complete phrase, including the small grammar words.

practice.prompt: Start a new conversation with Smarty. Choose the greeting, not an ending.
practice.explanation: Hello starts the conversation. Goodbye and Bye end it.

practice.prompt: Build a longer goodbye to Sam.
practice.explanation: Goodbye ends the conversation.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Hi is a short, friendly way to say hello.

practice.prompt: Ask the name question back using the short follow-up phrase.
practice.explanation: And you? asks the same question back after you have answered it.

story.hook: A new classmate joins the group. Which name will you hear?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: My name is Mia. And you?

questions.explanation: Find the line with the name or phrase in the question.
Use the speaker labels and the actual words in the dialogue.
Smarty ends the dialogue with Goodbye, Ben!

image.describe: A classroom table where Smarty the black cat sits with Mia, Sam and Ben, Sam leaning forward with a friendly smile.

mission.setup: A new classmate asks what to call you. Choose an imaginary name or nickname, then ask their name back.

turns.hint: Use My name is… or I’m… followed by a name.
Ask the question back using And you? or What’s your name?

lessons.title: Catch the name
lessons.canDo: Understand short introductions and politely ask for a repeat.
lessons.scenario: The classroom is a little noisy. Catch names, politely ask to hear them again, and thank the speaker.

items.note: The name usually comes after I’m or My name is. You do not have to understand every sound to catch a name.

grammar.title: Names after be
grammar.explanation: The name usually comes after I’m or My name is. You do not have to understand every sound to catch a name.

practice.prompt: A name was not clear. Start with a polite apology.
practice.explanation: Sorry politely signals that something was not heard or understood.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Again, please is a polite request to hear the words once more.

practice.prompt: Build the taught phrase in its natural word order.
practice.explanation: Put please after again to make this short repeat request polite.

practice.prompt: Thank Smarty after a repeat. Complete the phrase.
practice.explanation: Thank you acknowledges the person who helped by repeating the words.

practice.prompt: Sam repeats his name for you. Choose a short way to thank him.
practice.explanation: Thanks is another friendly way to thank the speaker.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: Say the complete phrase, including the small grammar words.

practice.prompt: Listen for the speaker’s name.
practice.explanation: I’m Ben introduces Ben. The greeting changes, but the name still comes after I’m.

practice.prompt: Listen for the speaker’s name.
practice.explanation: Listen for Sam after My name is.

practice.prompt: Choose the question you hear.
practice.explanation: What’s is the short form of What is.

practice.prompt: Choose the ending you hear.
practice.explanation: Goodbye signals that the conversation is ending.

story.hook: Smarty missed a name. Can the friends help him catch it?

questions.explanation: Find the line with the name or phrase in the question.
Use the speaker labels and the actual words in the dialogue.

questions.prompt: Who says My name is Sam, followed by Thanks?
questions.explanation: Sam gives his name and says Thanks in the last line.

image.describe: A noisy school classroom where Smarty the black cat cups a paw to his ear while Mia smiles and nods, with Sam waving nearby.

mission.setup: The classroom is a little noisy. Catch names, politely ask to hear them again, and thank the speaker.

turns.hint: Politely ask to hear the name again.
Thank the speaker after the repeat.

lessons.title: I am, you are
lessons.canDo: Use the right form of be in an introduction.
lessons.scenario: Smarty introduces fictional classmates. Confirm who each person is and introduce the pair together.

items.note: Use am with I, and are with you. In speech, I am often becomes I’m and you are becomes you’re. They mean the same thing.

grammar.title: I am. You are.
grammar.explanation: Use am with I, and are with you. In speech, I am often becomes I’m and you are becomes you’re. They mean the same thing.

practice.prompt: Confirm that the other person is Mia.
practice.explanation: You goes with are: You are Mia.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Use He is to introduce the fictional character Sam. He’s is the short form.

practice.prompt: Build the taught phrase in its natural word order.
practice.explanation: Use She is to introduce Mia. She’s is the short form.

practice.prompt: Use the form of be that goes with you.
practice.explanation: You are + a name. We do not say You am.

practice.prompt: Match each full form to its short form. They have the same meaning.
practice.explanation: The short forms express the same meaning as their full forms. The apostrophe marks missing letters.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: I am Sam and I’m Sam are both correct introductions.

practice.prompt: Choose the form of be for I: I ___ Sam.
practice.explanation: I goes with am: I am Sam.

practice.prompt: Which sentence means the same as I am Ben?
practice.explanation: I’m combines I and am. The apostrophe replaces the missing a.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Hi is a short, friendly way to say hello.

story.hook: Two classmates arrive. Can you introduce them together?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: He is Sam. She is Mia.

questions.explanation: Find the line with the name or phrase in the question.
Use the speaker labels and the actual words in the dialogue.

questions.prompt: Who says We are Mia and Sam?
questions.explanation: Mia introduces the pair using We are.

image.describe: A school corridor where Smarty the black cat points to Mia and Sam, who stand side by side and wave to each other.

mission.setup: Smarty introduces fictional classmates. Confirm who each person is and introduce the pair together.

turns.hint: Imagine Smarty is playing Mia. Confirm her name.
Introduce Mia or introduce the pair, Sam and Mia.

lessons.title: A quick reunion
lessons.canDo: Use time-of-day greetings while recalling earlier introductions.
lessons.scenario: Meet the same friends at different times of day and say that you will see them later.

practice.prompt: You see Mia in the morning. Choose the matching greeting.
practice.explanation: Good morning is the taught greeting for the morning. Use it before the afternoon.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for afternoon to identify Good afternoon.

practice.prompt: Build the taught phrase in its natural word order.
practice.explanation: Good evening is one phrase; put the greeting before the person’s name.

practice.prompt: It is evening. Complete the greeting.
practice.explanation: The time in this scene is evening, so complete Good evening.

practice.prompt: Say that you will see Ben later.
practice.explanation: See you later is a friendly way to end the conversation when you expect to meet again.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: Say the complete phrase, including the small grammar words.

practice.prompt: Start a new conversation with Smarty. Choose the greeting, not an ending.
practice.explanation: Hello starts the conversation. Goodbye and Bye end it. Start with a greeting, then introduce yourself or ask a question.

practice.prompt: Introduce yourself as Mia using My name is.
practice.explanation: My name is + a name. My tells us the name belongs to the speaker.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose a reply that gives your name.
practice.explanation: They are asking what to call you.

story.hook: The same friends meet again later. Which greeting changes?

questions.prompt: Who says Good morning to Smarty?
questions.explanation: Mia replies Good morning, Smarty.

questions.prompt: Who says Good afternoon to Sam?
questions.explanation: Use the speaker labels and the actual words in the dialogue.

questions.prompt: Who says See you later to Ben?
questions.explanation: Sam uses See you later, Ben!

image.describe: A school hallway with a sunny window, where Smarty the black cat and Mia wave at each other while Sam and Ben wave goodbye.

mission.setup: Meet the same friends at different times of day and say that you will see them later.

turns.hint: It is morning. Give a greeting back.
Say you will see your friend later, or give a goodbye.

grammar.title: Recall an introduction
grammar.explanation: I am; you are. The verb changes with the speaker. My name is… and I’m… are both accepted.

lessons.title: Where are you from?
lessons.canDo: Say where you are from and ask someone else.
lessons.scenario: Tell a new classmate where your imaginary character is from, then ask the question back. Countries are examples, never assumptions about learners.

items.note: I’m from… tells someone your country or place of origin. Where are you from? asks the same question back. Use a real or imaginary place for practice.

grammar.title: From + a place
grammar.explanation: I’m from… tells someone your country or place of origin. Where are you from? asks the same question back. Use a real or imaginary place for practice.

practice.prompt: Introduce your imaginary character as coming from Uzbekistan.
practice.explanation: From introduces the place you come from.

practice.prompt: Listen and choose the speaker’s country.
practice.explanation: Listen for the place after from.

practice.prompt: Build a question to ask where someone is from.
practice.explanation: Question order: Where + are + you + from?

practice.prompt: Say that your character comes from Brazil.
practice.explanation: Use I’m from… or I am from… followed by a place.

practice.prompt: Match each place with the sentence about that same place.
practice.explanation: The country after from tells you where the speaker comes from.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: Say the complete phrase, including the small grammar words.

practice.prompt: Start a new conversation with Smarty. Choose the greeting, not an ending.
practice.explanation: Hello starts the conversation. Goodbye and Bye end it.

practice.prompt: Introduce yourself as Mia using My name is.
practice.explanation: My name is + a name. My tells us the name belongs to the speaker.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Hi is a short, friendly way to say hello.

story.hook: Smarty has a visiting friend. Which country will you hear?

questions.explanation: Sam says I’m from Brazil.
Use the speaker labels and the actual words in the dialogue.
Mia asks the question back after the classmates give their countries.

image.describe: A classroom with a world map on the wall, where Smarty the black cat points at the map while Mia, Sam and Ben stand by it.

mission.setup: Tell a new classmate where your imaginary character is from, then ask the question back. Countries are examples, never assumptions about learners.

turns.hint: Use I’m from… or I am from… followed by a place.
Question order: Where + are + you + from?

lessons.title: Two new classmates
lessons.canDo: Understand a tiny conversation and follow who says what.
lessons.scenario: Smarty introduces a visiting friend. Exchange names and countries, then give a friendly reply.

items.note: Say Nice to meet you when you meet someone for the first time. You can reply Nice to meet you, too. Too means also here.

grammar.title: A friendly reply with too
grammar.explanation: Say Nice to meet you when you meet someone for the first time. You can reply Nice to meet you, too. Too means also here. They exchange names, ask about countries and say Nice to meet you.

practice.prompt: Say that you are pleased to meet Mia for the first time.
practice.explanation: Nice to meet you is a friendly phrase for a first meeting.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Too lets Sam say that he is also pleased to meet Mia.

practice.prompt: Build the taught phrase in its natural word order.
practice.explanation: This is introduces another person. My friend tells the listener how you know Sam.

practice.prompt: Show that you are also pleased to meet the person.
practice.explanation: Too means also here: you are also pleased to meet the person.

practice.prompt: Say that you are pleased to meet Mia for the first time.
practice.explanation: Recall the complete phrase from its teaching card.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: Say the complete phrase, including the small grammar words.

practice.explanation: Hello starts the conversation. Goodbye and Bye end it.

practice.prompt: Introduce yourself as Mia using My name is.
practice.explanation: My name is + a name. My tells us the name belongs to the speaker.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Hi is a short, friendly way to say hello.

story.hook: Smarty’s friend arrives. Where is he from? Read or listen. Look for each person’s name and country.

questions.explanation: Too lets Sam say that he is also pleased to meet Mia.

turns.hint: Too lets Sam say that he is also pleased to meet Mia.

lessons.title: Your turn with Smarty
lessons.canDo: Exchange names, origins and a short answer about feelings.
lessons.scenario: Check in with Smarty and classmates. Different feelings are all acceptable; nobody has to pretend to feel happy.

grammar.title: I am + a feeling
grammar.explanation: Use I am or I’m before a feeling. A complete reply can include Thank you and a question back.

practice.prompt: Ask a friend about their feelings.
practice.explanation: How are you? asks about the other person’s feelings.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Use I am or I’m before fine. Thank you makes this reply friendly.

practice.prompt: Build the taught phrase in its natural word order.
practice.explanation: The pattern is I am + a feeling. Keep am after I.

practice.prompt: Your imaginary character needs some rest. Complete the feeling.
practice.explanation: Tired is the feeling in this imaginary scene. Other feelings are valid in an open conversation.

practice.prompt: Ask Mia about her feelings, rather than stating your own feeling.
practice.explanation: How are you? is the taught question about feelings, not a statement about yourself.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: Say the complete phrase, including the small grammar words.

practice.prompt: Start a new conversation with Smarty. Choose the greeting, not an ending.
practice.explanation: Reply to a greeting with a greeting.

practice.prompt: Introduce yourself as Mia using My name is.
practice.explanation: A complete introduction includes My name is… or I’m… plus a name.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Hi is a short, friendly way to say hello.

practice.prompt: You need to leave. Finish the conversation.
practice.explanation: You can finish politely with Goodbye.

questions.explanation: Smarty says I’m tired.

questions.prompt: Who replies Nice to meet you, too?
questions.explanation: Nice to meet you, too is a friendly reply when you meet someone.

image.describe: A bright classroom where Smarty the black cat sits slumped and tired at a desk, while Mia and Sam smile and wave hello.

lessons.canDo: Ask for repetition or slower speech when a conversation is difficult.

grammar.title: A polite request
grammar.explanation: Can you…? makes a request. Please makes it polite. I don’t understand means I do not understand; ask to hear the words again.

practice.prompt: You missed a phrase. Ask to hear it again.
practice.explanation: Choose the phrase that fits this situation.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the words in this phrase, then match the whole utterance.

lessons.title: Meet someone new
lessons.canDo: Introduce yourself, exchange origins, ask about someone else and answer a student question.
lessons.scenario: Meet new fictional classmates. Introduce yourself, exchange origins, ask a question and say whether your character is a student.

items.note: Imagine you are meeting a new classmate. Write your own replies without answer tiles. A nickname and an imaginary place are fine. This checks the English pattern, not whether personal details are real.

grammar.title: Turn a statement into a question
grammar.explanation: I am a student is a statement. Are you a student? asks the other person. Reply Yes, I am or No, I am not.

practice.prompt: Your imaginary character is a student. Make a statement about yourself.
practice.explanation: I am a student is a statement about your imaginary character.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Are you a student? asks the other person. Listen for the question order.

practice.prompt: Build the taught phrase in its natural word order.
practice.explanation: Yes, I am is a short positive reply to Are you a student?

practice.prompt: Your imaginary character is not a student. Complete the reply.
practice.explanation: No, I am not is the short negative reply. Keep not after am.

practice.prompt: Make a complete statement saying that your imaginary character is a student.
practice.explanation: The complete statement includes a before student: I am a student.

practice.prompt: Say the phrase aloud. You can retry if recognition mishears you.
practice.explanation: Say the complete phrase, including the small grammar words.

practice.prompt: Start a new conversation with Smarty. Choose the greeting, not an ending.
practice.explanation: Hello starts the conversation. Goodbye and Bye end it.

practice.prompt: A new classmate joins. Build a question to ask their name.
practice.explanation: What’s your name? and What is your name? both work. Use your when you ask about the other person’s name.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the phrase you heard.
practice.explanation: Hi is a short, friendly way to say hello.

story.hook: A new classmate joins the group. Can you keep the conversation going?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: My name is Sam. I’m from Brazil.

questions.explanation: Find the line with the name or phrase in the question.
Use the speaker labels and the actual words in the dialogue.

questions.prompt: Who says they are a student, too?
questions.explanation: Find the matching line in the dialogue; use what the story actually says.

image.describe: A school courtyard with a bench, where Smarty the black cat, Mia and Sam sit together chatting and smiling, with Sam waving hello.

mission.setup: Imagine you are meeting a new classmate. Write your own replies without answer tiles. A nickname and an imaginary place are fine. This checks the English pattern, not whether personal details are real. You have introduced yourself and kept a short conversation going.

turns.hint: Use My name is… or I’m… and a name.
Use I’m from… or I am from… and a place.
Where are you from? asks about the other person.
Answer for your imaginary character. Yes and No are both valid.
